annotation.kind: constructive polynomial form of Lemma 4.2's exceptional-point approximation argument

assumptions: 0 < a < b and all exceptional nodes are positive, as in Lemma 4.2.
The nodes are pairwise distinct, matching the set {x_1,...,x_k} in the paper.
p is an arbitrary degree-n interval approximant to 1/x with error epsilon.
p56Correction is the degree-at-most-k reciprocal interpolant r constructed from phi, and p56ExtendedApproximant is the paper's corrected polynomial r plus the scaled product phi p.
p56IntervalFactor is an explicit valid choice of the constant depending only on a, b, and the exceptional points.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P56 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P56 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p56_t3_exceptional_point_approximation (k n : Nat) (a b epsilon : Real) (nodes : Fin k -> Real) (p : Polynomial Real) (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b) (hnodes : forall i, 0 < nodes i) (hinj : Function.Injective nodes) (hpdegree : p.natDegree <= n) (hpapprox : forall t, a <= t -> t <= b -> |t⁻¹ - Polynomial.eval t p| <= epsilon) : (p56ExtendedApproximant nodes p).natDegree <= n + k and (forall i, Polynomial.eval (nodes i) (p56ExtendedApproximant nodes p) = (nodes i)⁻¹) and forall t, a <= t -> t <= b -> |t⁻¹ - Polynomial.eval t (p56ExtendedApproximant nodes p)| <= p56IntervalFactor a b nodes * epsilon
formal_statement.plain_language: Show that the correction used in Lemma 4.2 preserves a controlled degree, interpolates 1/x at every exceptional point, and multiplies the interval error by one fixed endpoint-based constant.

informal_proof: The nodal product is nonzero at zero because every exceptional point is positive. Divide its nonconstant part by X to construct the reciprocal interpolant r and prove 1-xr(x)=c phi(x). This identity gives interpolation at every node and the exact corrected-error factorization. Bound each |t-x_i| on [a,b] by the larger endpoint distance, multiply the bounds, and combine them with the assumed error of p. Polynomial degree inequalities give the n+k bound.
informal_statement: Prove the constructive approximation step used in Lemma 4.2 to add finitely many exceptional spectral points without changing the exponential rate.

tier_rationale: The task requires constructing a reciprocal interpolation correction from a nodal product, proving its zero-value normalization and exact pointwise identity, establishing interpolation at an arbitrary finite family, controlling polynomial degrees through division and products, deriving an exact corrected-error factorization, and proving a uniform product bound from interval endpoints. The exact N proof has 191 physical lines and is at least as demanding as the lower validated T2/T3 workload rather than a short Mathlib import exercise. The exact L mathematical proof is byte-identical and uses no NumStability declaration, establishing that the frozen library provides no speedup.
